decision_matrix.permission_denied_local_bypass: pre_tool_call block fires on every tool, including MCP and delegated child: gate is host-wide. E3 (host hook) is viable as a first-mile enforcement point independent of our dispatcher.
decision_matrix.subagent_reached: gate reaches delegated children; no hole where a subagent can bypass the host gate.
decision_matrix.noninteractive_terminates: one-shot run exits 0 in ~24s; gate does not deadlock unattended runs (need a typed 'get baseline' path for the agent, but it fails gracefully, not hangs).
decision_matrix.fail_closed_on_raise: hook exception => tool blocked; gate cannot be silently switched off by a crash. Still requires external monitoring to distinguish 'gate raised' from 'gate idle', because silently-allow is impossible but silently-block is noisy.
decision_matrix.mcp_covered: MCP and built-in tools share one pre_tool_call hook; no per-type bypass.

architecture_recommendation.enforcement_point: E3 host pre_tool_call hook is technically sound and host-wide (covers main agent, subagents, built-in and MCP tools).
architecture_recommendation.required_support: a non-interactive 'get baseline' primed-allow mechanism so unattended/cron/subagent runs can pass the gate deliberately; external audit counter to catch silent fail-closed noise (too many blocks) and confirm gate liveness.
architecture_recommendation.complements: E1 (our launch wrapper) + E2 (DOM submit/admit requiring baseline receipt) still valuable; E3 closes the 'launched not by us' bypass. Recommend E1+E2 first, E3 as a hardening layer because it requires per-profile isolation, TTL cleanup, and operator exit-hatch.
architecture_recommendation.not_proven_by_gate: agent terminal cannot bypass MCP coverage (dedicated test not run); other hosts (opencode etc.) may differ; long-project reliability needs live operation.
